paragraphs.text: A cake of [Fuding white tea](fujian-white:definition) from 2009. Fuding is a hilly coastal city in the north-east of Fujian, by the Zhejiang border. Its white tea carries a protected origin name in China and is tied to Taimu Mountain. Like all white tea, the leaf was only [withered and dried](white:definition), never fixed or rolled, before it was pressed.

[Pressed white tea](fujian-white:cakes) was still new in 2009. Cakes began in that decade and spread around 2010, because a cake keeps and travels more easily than loose leaf. The year on a cake can mark when it was pressed rather than when it was picked. At seventeen years this cake is well past the seven of the trade's saying, [one year tea, three years medicine, seven years treasure](fujian-white:ageing). That is a saying, though, and no agreed number of years makes a white tea aged. As white tea ages, its liquor turns deeper and redder.

brewing.text: Gongfu style, use about 1 gram of leaf to 15 to 25 ml of water, for example 5 grams in a 100 to 110 ml gaiwan; weigh it, since the leaf is light and bulky. Silver Needle and young, delicate tea take water below the boil, about 75 to 90°C; older, leafier or aged tea takes water at or near the boil. Start with a steep of 10 to 45 seconds and add a few seconds each round. An aged cake is often rinsed quickly first, and older pressed tea can be simmered on the stove, about 5 grams to 500 ml for 3 to 10 minutes; young, delicate tea is not.

notice.text: Jujube or dried dates, herbs and medicine, wood, honey and dried fruit, a deeper, redder liquor, a thicker, rounder body, and less lift in the scent than a young tea.
